open_questions: Centroid is inconclusive due to no clear difference image, so on-target location is not directly imaged but is supported by low-blend ratio and steady depth; follow-up centroiding would confirm.

Low SNR 10.14 with only 3 transits leaves room for depth mis-estimate; additional high-SNR transits will refine period, impact parameter b 0.8789, and rule out spot harmonic coincidence with 15.0 d rotation period which is close to 11.9 d.
dossier.public_summary: A flat-bottomed 2765 ppm dip every 11.9 days repeats in two TESS sectors at the same depth and implies a 3.4 Earth-radius planet. No nearby stars within a TESS pixel can mimic the signal and there is no significant second eclipse or variable depth. The star's 15-day spin and few transits prevent a final proof, but the signal is best explained as a planet on the target.

reasons.why: Strongly flat-bottomed (negative V shape) favours a planetary transit over a grazing stellar eclipse.
Planet-sized (≈3.4 Earth radii) well below stellar regime, with undiluted depth 2786 ppm.
Depth steady across sectors (per-sector 2789 +/- 347 ppm and 2670 +/- 482 ppm, depth_change_pct 4.36) with transit_depths p_consistent 0.089 for 3 transits.
No Gaia star within one TESS pixel (21 arcsec) can cause the dip with <=25% eclipse, closest that could is 51.4 arcsec needing 0.3001 eclipse, and contratio 0.00788 is low.

No significant secondary at 11.9 d (well below 5) and phase_curve amplitude 173.6 ppm ratio_to_depth 0.06279 low, no stellar companion signature; odd_even diff_sigma 1.999 flagged but sector_oe_max_sigma 2.204 and sector_oe_same_sign_share 1 show no consistent odd/even from spot modulation.
